coupling: Commit 026e091 ('Remove unnecessary resize') right-sizes userDataDecoder's scratch DataBuf from 100 bytes to the 5 bytes every code path existing at that point actually uses (two 4-byte reads plus a nul terminator at index 4); audited against the whole function, the shrink is provably safe, so the diff reads as correct maintenance. Commit 66c95a5 ('Nul-terminate strings') splits the NCHD (Nikon maker-note-type) atom out of the shared readString branch into its own branch that reads the fixed-length 8-byte identifier into that same scratch buffer and nul-terminates it at offset 8 - written in the commit's own idiom (identical to the five other read-N/write_uint8(N,0) conversions it makes) and safe against the 100-byte buffer the decoder had before commit 026e091. Neither diff is wrong in isolation: with only the first edit, NCHD is still decoded via readString (which allocates its own buffer), so nothing exceeds the 5-byte buffer; with only the second edit, the 8-byte read and the offset-8 terminator fit the 100-byte buffer. Composed, readOrThrow(buf.data(), 8) performs an 8-byte memcpy into the 5-byte heap allocation inside MemIo::read, a heap-buffer-overflow write that ASan reports before the bounds-checked DataBuf::write_uint8(8, 0) can throw. The fix is non-local because the two facts needed for a correct repair - the buffer's capacity (5, introduced by the first commit) and the branch's requirement (9 bytes, introduced by the second) - live in different diffs; each commit's diff is self-consistent and correct given only its own context, so the minimal repair (give the NCHD branch an adequately sized buffer, or decode it with a size-aware read such as readString) cannot be derived from, or validated against, either single diff alone. Counterfactual builds confirm the delocalization: trees carrying only the first or only the second edit both run the PoC cleanly (no ASan report); only the composition aborts.
